I've never seen a cast iron wok that I can recall. But I have seen a number of mild carbon steel ones, and mild carbon steel will season just like cast iron. The main difference between mild carbon steel and cast iron is carbon levels. By design, a proper wok is too thin to be made of cast iron. The best quality wok I have seen is a hand hammered one, but it was pretty pricey. I'd not recommend any in stainless, stainless is alloyed with chromium (and nickle) and chromium is not good for you. Over time, it can leach out of the stainless under heat. Some stainless also has other things in the alloy that makes it very bad for cooking. Stainless cutlery other than cutting knives are ok, as they are almost always high nickle/low chromium, and not subject to high levels of heat to cause leeching. Carbon steel for any knife that you would want to cut with, stainless can take an edge, but not as well as carbon, and won't hold it for very long either.
